SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY. JUL 18 1938

A Pan-Asianism Spokesman
MITSURU TOYAMA ADVOCATES REVOLT
OF EASTERN PEOPLES TO RID THE
ORIENT OF WHITE INFLUENCE
By WILLIAM HENRY CHAMBERLIN
(Christian Science Monitor Magazine)

IT was with more than usual interest that I looked forward to the prospect of a meeting with Mitsuru Toyama. For this Nestor of Japanese nationalism, who has now passed the Biblical fourscore years of human existence, is more than a political leader; he is a distinctive personality in a country where regimentation does not make for strongly marked individualism. He is even more than a personality: he has become a sort of legendary figure, a human pillar of the ideals of Old Japan.

TOYAMA'S name in Japan suggests a host of associations, glamorous, mysterious, violent. One thinks of the two secret societies in which he played a leading part, the Black Ocean Society, founded when he was still a young man, and the Black Dragon Society, both designed as spearheads of Japan's continental expansion. One recalls the bomb which badly wounded one of the leading statesmen of the Meiji Era, (Count) Okuma, when he was not moving as fast as impatient nationalists desired in the direction of abolishing foreign extra-territorial privileges. The bomb was thrown by one of Toyama's henchmen.

Another incident, characteristic of the career of a man who has always cultivated warm Pan-Asian sympathies and has never showed undue regard for constituted authority, occurred during the World War. The British Government was endeavoring to obtain the extradition from Japan of two Indian revolutionaries who were accused of terrorist offenses. The Japanese authorities were ready to surrender them; but they suddenly "disappeared." There was a strong suspicion that the wanted Indians were concealed in Toyama's house. If this suspicion was true, the house was searched in vain. The Indians were never found or handed over, and one is still living in Japan as a naturalized citizen.

I CALLED on Toyama with a Japanese-speaking interpreter early in the morning, for the Nationalist patriarch believes in going to bed and rising early. Everything about the little undistinguished house where he lives suggested old-fashioned frugality and austerity. The hallways and corridors were freezing cold in the intense Tokyo winter and the room in which Toyama holds his daily receptions (the scene of persons visit him) was very scantily heated by one or two hibachi, or little charcoal braziers.

Around a low table Toyama and several guests were seated in the familiar Japanese cross-legged posture. Most of them were asking for his intervention on personal business matters, and Toyama, who has the feudal sense of obligation of lord after his vassals, listened to the tale of each petitioner, writing out a letter of introduction to the South Manchuria Railway or some other organization which might be able to help the suppliant.

THERE were no particularly distinguished callers at the time of my visit; but it is generally understood that such eminent statesmen as Foreign Minister Hirota find it well worth-while to cultivate good personal relations with the venerable prophet of Japanese nationalism. When my own turn came to address Toyama, I was impressed by the mildness both of manner and sentiment which characterized this man, whose name was so closely associated with deeds of violence. The Sino-Japanese conflict he brushed aside as mere "misunderstanding between brothers" and he discoursed so eloquently on the beauties of peace and the futility of force that one might almost imagine oneself listening to the views of Gandhi or Tolstoy. When I asked him outright whether he believed in nonviolence, however, Toyama offered some reservations:

"There are times when the use of force is unavoidable," he said. "To defend one's country, for instance, or to extend the Kodo (Imperial Way, the traditional code of ethics of Japan). But force, if it is necessary, should always be employed for the sincere purpose of getting rid of strife in the world; for it is not the essence of human nature to fight."

I SOON discovered that Toyama was a seer rather than a politician or economist. Many of his answers were couched in typically Oriental vagueness, and they were delivered after a long or shorter period of silent contemplation. One subject, however, which evidently struck a responsive chord, was the question of Pan-Asianism and Japan's role in promoting it.

"It is only a question of time until White rule will disappear from the Orient," he declared. "I am glad to have done what I could to hasten the coming of this time. It is Japan's destiny to help the revolt of the Eastern peoples in order to get rid of alien Western influence. Then will come a brotherhood of Asiatic peoples which will show the world something new in the realm of civilization."

On the question of the Soviet Union, usually a very literal red rag to a Japanese of conservative views, Mr. Toyama expressed himself coolly and moderately.

"It doesn't concern us if Communism prevails in Russia," he declared. "If they try to force Communism on us, of course, we shall resist it. But I do not believe that the Soviet Government has any aggressive designs against Japan at present. And there is no reason why we should not have friendly relations with Russia, provided she respects our interests in Manchuria and Mongolia."

In response to a question about what sort of internal measures of reform he favored for Japan, Mr. Toyama revealed the fact that he is not a politician or an economist, with a clearcut program, but rather a moral philosopher, according to his own lights.

"All Japanese are brothers," he began. "Great or small, rich or poor, we are all children and subjects of His Imperial Majesty. The state should control private economic life for the general welfare, but without using force. What is most needed is that all Japanese should practice fraternal love in their relations with each other."

THE interview was ended. With ceremonious courtesy, the venerable leader of the formidable ronin, or Japanese political adventurers, autographed one of his photographs and presented it to me and accompanied me to the genkan, or entrance of his house, with a formal bow which I awkwardly endeavored to reciprocate.

The militant Pan-Asianism, to which Mitsuru Toyama has devoted so much of his life, today possesses a very definite political significance. Gen. Iwane Matsui, commander of the Japanese forces in the Shanghai-Nanking area, is an ardent Pan-Asian. Before the outbreak of the present hostilities, I had a long talk with General Matsui, who pronounced himself a believer in the slogan, "Asia for the Asiatics," and expressed the belief that the white race should withdraw politically from Asia. Another influential Japanese political figure, Admiral Nobumasa Suetsugu, who is Home Minister in Prince Konoye's Cabinet, recently expressed the following views in a magazine interview:

"Unless the colored races are rescued from their miserable slavery under the yoke of the White peoples, there can be no world peace. This is my conviction, and I am ready to proclaim it to the world without hesitation."

PAN-ASIANISM would be a still more effective force if the Japanese had been able to repress or moderate their own impulse to dominate any part of Asia that came under their influence. Formosa and Korea, Manchuria, and now North China offer convincing evidence that "Asia for the Asiatics," in practice, is apt to mean, "Asia for the Japanese." But the dynamic force of the idea as a factor in Japan's expansion cannot be mistaken; and it perhaps more likely to increase than to diminish with the passing of time.

S.U.
S.I. / SK

泛亚主义代言人
头山满鼓动东方民族起义以清除白人影响
作者：威廉·亨利·钱伯林
（《基督教科学箴言报》杂志）

我怀着比平时更浓厚的兴趣，期待着与头山满会面的前景。这位日本民族主义的元老，如今已年过八旬（圣经所称的高寿），他不仅是一位政治领袖；在这个整齐划一并不利于形成鲜明个人主义的国家里，他是一个个性独特的人物。他甚至比一个有个性的人更重要：他已成为某种传奇人物，是旧日本理想的中流砥柱。

在日本，提到头山的名字，就会让人联想到一系列迷人、神秘且暴力的事物。人们会想到他在其中发挥领导作用的两个秘密社团：一个是他在年轻时创立的黑龙会的前身玄洋社，另一个是黑龙会，两者均旨在作为日本大陆扩张的先锋。人们还会想起那枚炸伤明治时代主要政治家之一大隈（伯爵）的炸弹，当时他废除外国治外法权特权的步伐未能满足急躁的民族主义者的期望。那枚炸弹是由头山的一名手下投掷的。

另一件事例典型地反映了一个人的生涯，此人一直培养热烈的泛亚同情心，且从未对既定权威表现出过度的尊重，这件事发生在世界大战期间。英国政府正试图从日本引渡两名被指控犯有恐怖主义罪行的印度革命者。日本当局准备移交他们；但他们突然“失踪”了。有人强烈怀疑这些被通缉的印度人藏在头山的家中。如果这一怀疑属实，搜查也是徒劳的。这些印度人从未被找到或移交，其中一人至今仍作为归化公民居住在日本。

清晨，我带着一名懂日语的口译员去拜访头山，因为这位国民党（此处指日本国家主义/民族主义，原文Nationalist应指日本国粹主义者，但结合上下文及当时语境，译为“国家主义”或保留“民族主义”更妥，鉴于后文提到Old Japan，此处指日本传统民族主义）家长信奉早睡早起。他居住的这座不起眼的小房子的一切都暗示着老式的节俭和简朴。在东京严冬中，走廊和过道冷得刺骨，头山每日接见访客（人们来访的场景）的房间仅靠一两个火钵（小型炭盆）微弱供暖。

头山和几位客人围坐在一张矮桌旁，摆出熟悉的日本盘腿坐姿。大多数人都在请求他干预个人商务事宜，而头山怀着封建时代领主对家臣般的义务感，倾听了每位请愿者的陈述，并写下一封介绍信，推荐他们去找南满洲铁道株式会社或其他可能帮助求助者的组织。

在我访问期间，并没有特别显赫的访客；但众所周知，像外相广田这样的杰出政治家认为，与这位德高望重的日本民族主义先知保持良好的私人关系是非常值得的。当轮到我向头山致辞时，令我印象深刻的是这位名字与暴力行为紧密相连的人所表现出的温和举止和情感。他将中日冲突轻描淡写地称为兄弟间的“误会”，并如此雄辩地论述和平之美和武力的徒劳，以至于人们几乎以为自己正在聆听甘地或托尔斯泰的观点。然而，当我直截了当地问他是否相信非暴力时，头山提出了一些保留意见：

“有时使用武力是不可避免的，”他说。“例如，为了保卫国家，或为了弘扬皇道（Kodo，日本传统的道德准则）。但是，如果有必要使用武力，应始终出于消除世界纷争的真诚目的；因为好斗并非人性的本质。”

我很快发现，头山更像是一位先知，而非政治家或经济学家。他的许多回答都带有典型的东方模糊性，并且是在经过或长或短的静默沉思后才说出的。然而，有一个主题显然引起了共鸣，那就是泛亚主义以及日本在促进泛亚主义中的作用问题。

“白人统治从东方消失只是时间问题，”他宣称。“我很高兴能为加速这一时刻的到来尽我所能。日本的命运是帮助东方民族起义，以摆脱外来西方的影响。随后将出现一个亚洲民族兄弟会，向世界展示文明领域的新气象。”

关于苏联的问题，这通常是对持保守观点的日本人来说非常敏感的刺激物，头山先生表现得冷静而适度。

“如果共产主义在俄国盛行，这与我们要无关，”他宣称。“如果他们试图将共产主义强加给我们，我们当然会抵抗。但我认为苏联政府目前对日本没有任何侵略意图。只要俄国尊重我们在满洲和蒙古的利益，我们就没有理由不与俄国保持友好关系。”

在回答他赞成日本进行何种内部改革措施的问题时，头山先生揭示了他并非拥有明确纲领的政治家或经济学家，而是一位按照自己见解行事的道德哲学家。

“所有日本人都是兄弟，”他开始说道。“无论大小、贫富，我们都是天皇陛下的子民和臣民。国家应为普遍福利控制私人经济生活，但不使用武力。最迫切需要的是，所有日本人在彼此关系中践行博爱。”

采访结束了。这位令人生畏的浪人（即日本政治冒险家）的 venerable 领袖以仪式般的礼貌，在其中一张照片上签名并赠送给我，并陪我走到玄关（房屋入口），向我正式鞠躬，我则笨拙地试图回礼。

头山满毕生致力于好战的泛亚主义，如今具有非常明确的政治意义。驻上海-南京地区日军司令松井石根将军是一位热情的泛亚主义者。在目前敌对行动爆发之前，我曾与松井将军进行过长时间交谈，他自称信奉“亚洲属于亚洲人”的口号，并表示相信白人种族应在政治上撤出亚洲。另一位有影响力的日本政治人物、近卫文麿内阁的内务大臣末次信正海军上将，最近在杂志采访中表达了以下观点：

“除非有色人种从白人种族枷锁下的悲惨奴役中获救，否则就不可能有世界和平。这是我的信念，我准备毫不犹豫地向世界宣告。”

如果日本人能够抑制或缓和其支配任何受其影响的亚洲地区的冲动，泛亚主义将成为一股更有效的力量。台湾、朝鲜、满洲以及现在的华北提供了令人信服的证据，表明在实践中，“亚洲属于亚洲人”往往意味着“亚洲属于日本人”。但是，作为一种推动日本扩张的因素，这一思想的动态力量是不容误认的；而且随着时间的推移，它更有可能增强而不是减弱。

S.U.
S.I. / SK

'Asia For The Asiatics" Warcry Of Nippon
Pan-Asian Society; Ideas Gaining Strength

General Matsui Directs Activities Of Japan
Movement To Run Affairs In Far East;
Sympathizers Said Found In China

Philippines Future Closely Watched

A FEDERATION of Asiatic nations, cemented by common cultural ties, and looking toward Japan for leadership, is the ideal of the Dai Asia Kyokai, or Great Asia Association of Japan, in which Gen. Iwane Matsui, former commander of the Japanese Army in Formosa is a leading figure.

Even since Japan left the League of Nations, Pan-Asian ideas have been gaining strength in the Army and among some conservative intellectuals.

The Great Asia Association is the most tangible agency for promoting these ideas and General Matsui recently set forth his ideas about the background and prospects of Pan-Asianism:

"The idea of the League of Nations is good, but it has proved powerless in practice. What is necessary is to begin with smaller associations of countries, bound together by historical and cultural ties. An Asiatic League of Nations, based on the slogan, 'Asia for the Asiatics' would be a step in the right direction.'

"Europeanization" Blamed

In response to a suggestion that the present differences between Japan and its largest Asiatic neighbor, China, might obstruct the realization of the Pan-Asiatic ideal, General Matsui observed:

"The disagreement between Japan and China concerns temporary questions, which can be settled without war. Europeanization is really at the bottom of the trouble. If this were eliminated, Japan and China, two oriental countries with so much in common in their cultural history, could easily come to an understanding.

"I recently made a long trip in China and found sympathizers with the Pan-Asian idea in all the large cities which I visited, especially among the older and more mature Chinese. The students are less favorable to the idea; they have been exposed to too many unsettling foreign influences, such as democracy, communism and fascism."

* * *

Wide Following

GENERAL Matsui declared that the Pan-Asiatic idea had followers in British India, Afghanistan, French Indo-China and the Philippines, mentioning especially Prof. Pio Duran in the latter country. Professor Duran believes that the future welfare of the Philippines will be best assured if close relations are cultivated with Japan. Branches of the Great Asia Association have been formed in Korea and in Formosa; and the movement, according to General Matsui, has found sympathizers in Tientsin and Canton, although the authorities in the latter city have forbidden any organization in this connection.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年3月5日，星期五

“亚洲属于亚洲人”是日本的战争口号
泛亚协会；思想日益增强

松井将军指导日本运动以掌管远东事务；
据称在中国找到同情者

密切关注菲律宾的未来

一个由共同文化纽带维系、并视日本为领导的亚洲国家联邦，是大亚细亚协会（Dai Asia Kyokai，即日本大亚细亚协会）的理想，前日本驻台湾军司令松井石根将军是该协会的核心人物。

自从日本退出国联以来，泛亚思想在军队和一些保守知识分子中日益增强。

大亚细亚协会是促进这些思想的最具体机构，松井将军最近阐述了他对泛亚主义背景和前景的看法：

“国联的理念是好的，但在实践中已被证明无力。有必要从由历史和文化纽带联系在一起的小型国家联盟开始。基于‘亚洲属于亚洲人’口号的亚洲国联将是朝着正确方向迈出的一步。”

归咎于“欧化”

针对有人提出日本与其最大的亚洲邻国中国之间的当前分歧可能会阻碍泛亚理想的实现，松井将军指出：

“日本和中国之间的分歧涉及暂时性问题，可以在不发动战争的情况下解决。麻烦的根源实际上是欧化。如果消除这一点，日本和中国这两个在文化史上有很多共同点的东方国家，很容易达成共识。

“我最近在中国进行了长途旅行，在我访问的所有大城市中都发现了泛亚思想的同情者，尤其是在年长和更成熟的中国人中间。学生对该想法的支持度较低；他们受到了太多不安定的外国影响，如民主、共产主义和法西斯主义。”

* * *

广泛的追随者

松井将军宣称，泛亚思想在英属印度、阿富汗、法属印度支那和菲律宾都有追随者，特别提到了菲律宾的皮奥·杜兰教授。杜兰教授认为，如果与日本建立密切关系，菲律宾未来的福祉将得到最佳保障。大亚细亚协会的分会已在朝鲜和台湾成立；据松井将军称，该运动在天津和广州也找到了同情者，尽管广州当局禁止任何此类组织。

泛亚主义思想正通过该协会散发的小册子、讲座及其他形式的宣传活动，取得缓慢但稳步的进展。

亚洲人的亚洲

在大亚细亚协会秘书中谷武世（Takeyo Nakatani）教授题为《亚洲人的亚洲：这意味着什么？》的小册子中，可以找到对该协会目标的有力而直率的陈述。中谷教授以如下措辞非常清晰地提出了日本霸权的思想：

“为目前混乱的亚洲局势带来秩序与重建，是主要落在日本肩上的责任……日本被要求动用其所有力量——文化的、政治的、经济的，以及在必要时的军事力量——以实现亚洲的统一和全面重建。”

中谷教授在其“亚洲人的亚洲”口号中看到了政治、经济和文化的含义。在他看来，今天的亚洲是一个欧洲人的亚洲，一个白人的亚洲，因此是一个“迷失的亚洲”。“真正控制中国政治和经济的是西方的帝国主义意志。”因此，实现亚洲人亚洲的首要有效条件，是整个亚洲大陆上西方影响的终结。既然日本已从一个被中谷教授称为“白人国家联盟”的国际联盟成员，转变为一个“彻底充满亚洲意识并以‘回到亚洲’为口号所激励”的国家，日本人如今便是亚洲联邦理念的最主要支持者。

作为经济单元

在经济方面，中谷教授呼吁“终止西方资本主义对亚洲及其资源的持续剥削”，并主张“形成作为一个整体的亚洲经济单元”。在文化领域，他认为亚洲各国正在拒绝西方模式，回归其古老的精神理念，并在此引用了印度圣雄甘地的运动。他预测，“未来的政治将由联合在一起的大型国家集团之间的共存与合作构成——诸如泛欧联盟、南北美洲联盟、苏联、亚洲联邦等集团。”

不应高估这一泛亚主义学说在日本以外的意义。它在中国这里确实鲜有支持，因为绝大多数受过教育的阶层将日本视为对中国行政主权和领土完整的主要威胁。但是，松井将军绝非日本高级军事领导人中唯一对日本作为“亚洲人治亚洲”运动的驱动力之使命怀有近乎神秘信仰的人。如果本世纪见证日本帝国的扩张，泛亚主义可能会成为一种道德口号，其对某些类型的日本人心灵的鼓舞作用，就如同吉卜林（Kipling）的“白人的负担”对坚信帝国统治福祉的英国信徒一样。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, MARCH 18, 1936 / 18 3 36

Matsui Tells
Principles Of
Pan-Asianism

General Says China And
Japan Must Get Down
“To Fundamentals”

DOESN’T SEEK
WEST EXCLUSION

Termed Basic Idea
Behind Nippon
Military

It is imperative that both China
and Japan get down to fun-
damentals before a real basis for
understanding and co-operation
may be reached, General Iwane
Matsui, Japan’s leading exponent
of the doctrine of Pan-Asianism,
told a CHINA PRESS reporter yester-
day in an interview at the Japanese
Consulate-General.

General Matsui, who arrived here
recently from South China, and
who returned Sunday from Nan-
king, will sail for Japan today on
the s.s. Nagasaki Maru for Japan.
In Nanking General Matsui had in-
terviews with General Chiang Kai-
shek, President of the Executive
Yuan, and General Chang Chun,
Foreign Minister. Yesterday he
was reported to have conferred
with Mr. T. V. Soong, Presi-
dent of the National Economic
Council, and Mayor Wu Teh-chen.

“Pan-Asianism,” General Matsui
explained through an interpreter.
“originated 40 years ago when Dr.
Sun Yat-sen visited Japan and
presented his ideas to a number of
Japanese leaders.

Similar Movements Abroad

“Since then, Pan-Asianism has
become the fundamental ideology
of the Japanese military and it is
with this doctrine as a basis that
the relations between Japan and
China must be worked out as a
whole. This does no mean that
China will be dominated by Japan.
I am seeking a co-ordination of all
the forces of good—cultural, psy-
chological, ethical—for the fun-
damental well-being of Asia, just
as there is a similar fundamental
policy and system in Europe and
in North and South America.

“Again, this movement does not
mean the exclusion of the West
from the Orient. We seek to bring
peace through the co-operation of
all the peoples of Asia. We re-
cognize the contributions that the
West has brought to the East.”

Back To Fundamentals

Asked what specific concrete pro-
posals he had in mind to bring
about the realization of his pro-
gram, General Matsui declared:
“The people of Asia must get back
to fundamentals. They must do
away with suspicion and antagon-
ism.”

When the question was repeated,
General Matsui suggested that talks
and personal contacts should be
made. “We must get down to
fundamentals,” he explained.
“Great progress has been made in
advancing the movement in “Man-
chukuo.” Amoy, Foochow and Pei-
ping also have Pan-Asia groups.
The movement, however, should be
made to include people who are
more representative of Japan and
and China.” General Matsui ad-
mitted that the doctrine has not
been supported by any leaders in
China.

Questioned again as to specific
ways in which the movement was
to be spread, the interpreter said:
“The General has ideas, but he is
not ready just yet to put them in
practice. We must get back to
fundamentals, you know.’

The reporter wanted to know
what “fundamentals” meant in
General Matsui’s explanation but
the question was politely ignored.

Suspicion Of Motives

Commenting on the lack of sup-
port of the movement in China,
General Matsui remarked: “Among
the younger generation and present
leaders in China there is suspicions
of Japan’s motives. In fact, many
Chinese fear ulterior motives in re-
spect to Japanese policy towards

China. China has always considered
herself the Celestial Kingdom and
looked on everyone else as bar-
barians. This is one of the points
upon which an understanding must
be reached.”

Through his interpreter, General
Matsui indicated that he does not
endorse any so-called “Asiatic Mon-
roe Doctrine,” nor is he an expon-
ent of an economic bloc between
Japan, China and “Manchukuo.”

“Japan has progressed much in
recent years and in the Japanese
mind there is a tendency to hold
China in contempt because she has
not enjoyed material progress.
These ideas must also be corrected.

“True, there are faults on both
sides. We must go to the roots of
these problems and arrive at a
fundamental and great understand-
ing. The present differences be-
tween China and Japan are only of
recent origin. Close co-operation is
fundamental between the two na-
tions and we must return to this,”
General Matsui said and the inter-
view concluded.

General Matsui delivered a lec-
ture on the subject to the Koyu
Club, composed of graduates of the
Tung Wen College, yesterday after-
noon.

《字林西报》，1936年3月18日，星期三 / 18 3 36

松井阐述
泛亚主义
原则

将军称中日必须
回归“根本”

并非寻求
排斥西方

被称为日本
军方背后的
基本理念

在中日双方能够达成真正的理解与合作基础之前，双方必须回归根本，日本泛亚主义学说的主要倡导者松井石根（Iwane Matsui）将军昨日在日本总领事馆接受《字林西报》记者采访时如是说。

松井将军近期从中国南方抵达此处，并于周日从南京返回，他将于今日乘坐长崎丸号轮船启程前往日本。在南京，松井将军会见了行政院院长蒋介石将军和外交部长张群将军。据报，他昨日还与全国经济委员会主席宋子文先生及市长吴铁城先生进行了会谈。

“泛亚主义，”松井将军通过翻译解释道，“起源于40年前孙中山博士访问日本并向多位日本领导人提出其理念之时。

国外的类似运动

“此后，泛亚主义已成为日本军方的基本意识形态，中日关系必须以此学说为基础进行整体规划。这并不意味着中国将被日本支配。我正在寻求协调所有良善力量——文化的、心理的、伦理的——以谋求亚洲的根本福祉，正如欧洲以及南北美洲也有类似的基本政策和体系。

“再者，这一运动并不意味着将西方排除出东方。我们寻求通过亚洲所有人民的合作带来和平。我们承认西方为东方带来的贡献。”

回归根本

当被问及为实现其计划有何具体的具体提议时，松井将军宣称：“亚洲人民必须回归根本。他们必须消除猜疑和敌意。”

当这个问题被再次提出时，松井将军建议应进行会谈和个人接触。“我们必须回归根本，”他解释道。“在推进‘满洲国’的运动方面已取得巨大进展。厦门、福州和北平也有泛亚团体。然而，该运动应吸纳更具日本和中国代表性的人士。”松井将军承认，该学说未得到中国任何领导人的支持。

当再次被问及传播该运动的具体方式时，翻译说道：“将军有一些想法，但他尚未准备好将其付诸实践。你知道，我们必须回归根本。”

记者想知道松井将军解释中的“根本”意味着什么，但该问题被礼貌地忽略了。

对动机的猜疑

在评论该运动在中国缺乏支持时，松井将军 remarked：“在中国年轻一代和现任领导人中，存在对日本动机的猜疑。事实上，许多中国人担心日本对华政策背后别有用心。中国一直自视为天朝上国，并将其他人视为蛮夷。这是必须达成理解的要点之一。”

通过他的翻译，松井将军表示他不支持任何所谓的“亚洲门罗主义”，也不是日本、中国和“满洲国”之间经济集团的倡导者。

“日本近年来进步很大，在日本人的思想中，有一种因中国未享受物质进步而轻视中国的倾向。这些想法也必须纠正。

“的确，双方都有过错。我们必须深入这些问题的根源，达成根本性的重大理解。中日目前的分歧仅是近期产生的。两国之间的紧密合作是根本，我们必须回归于此，”松井将军说道，采访随之结束。

昨日下午，松井将军向由同文书院毕业生组成的交游俱乐部（Koyu Club）就这一主题发表了演讲。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, MARCH 14, 1936

Matsui Gives Panacea
For Better Relations

“Criticize Yourself, Be Lenient
With Others,” He Opines

NANKING, Mar. 13.—(Central).—
“Be strict and severe in criticizing
oneself, but be liberal and lenient
in criticizing others” is the panacea
for the present Sino-Japanese im-
passe suggested by General Iwane
Matsui, former member of the Jap-
anese Supreme War Council and an
ardent advocate of Pan-Asianism,
in an interview with local press
representatives today.

General Matsui made several
trips to China during recent years
turning to good account his earlier
connections with the present-day
Chinese government leaders. He
arrived here yesterday after an
extensive tour to South China where
he saw Mr. Hu Han-min, recently
elected Chairman of the Standing
Committee of the Central Execu-
tive Committee, Mr. Hsiao Fu-chen,
Mr. Chow Lu and other leaders of
the Southwest.

To General Matsui’s mind the
present diplomatic and political es-
trangement between China and
Japan is not fundamentally import-
ant. Rather it is the thought and
attitude of the two peoples towards
each other, which should be culti-
vated and promoted. But when
asked how he proposed to separate
politics from racial feelings and
thoughts, he smiled and became
non-committal.

Physically Alike

Speaking of affinity physical and
otherwise between the Chinese and
Japanese he pointed to his Chinese
interviewers and then at himself
with an articulate gesture asking,
“Who can tell any difference be-
tween us?”

Preceding General Matsui said
that he is optimistic about the
future of Sino-Japanese relations,
although he admitted that it takes
time for the realization of Pan-
Asianism.

General Matsui was the guest of
honor at a luncheon party given by
General Chang Chun, Minister of
Foreign Affairs, today. Tomorrow
he will call on Gen. Chiang Kai-shek,
President of the Executive Yuan.
On Sunday he will leave for Shang-
hai to see Mr. T. V. Soong, Chair-
man of the Board of Directors of
the Bank of China, and Mayor Wu
Te-chen of Greater Shanghai. From
Shanghai he will sail for Japan on
March 18.

Not Going North

General Matsui is not visiting
North China this time. When ask-
ed if it wasn’t because of the lack
of need for promoting better Sino-
Japanese relations in North China,
he smiled and significantly answer-
ed with the question: “Hasn’t every
question been settled in North
China?”

《字林西报》，1936年3月14日，星期六

松井开出改善
关系良方

“严以律己，宽以待人”，他认为

南京，3月13日.—（中央社）.—“严以律己，宽以待人”是前日本最高战争会议成员、泛亚主义热忱倡导者松井石根将军今日在接受当地媒体代表采访时，为当前中日僵局提出的良方。

近年来，松井将军多次访华，充分利用了他与当今中国政府领导人的早期联系。他在对华南进行广泛巡视后于昨日抵达此处，期间会见了最近当选为中央执行委员会常务委员会主席的胡汉民先生、萧佛成先生、邹鲁先生以及其他西南领导人。

在松井将军看来，目前中日之间的外交和政治疏远并非根本重要。更重要的是两国人民彼此间的思想和态度，这需要培养和促进。但当被问及他打算如何将政治与种族情感和思想分开时，他笑了笑，未作明确表态。

外貌相似

在谈到中日之间在外貌及其他方面的亲缘关系时，他指向采访他的中国人，然后指向自己，做出一个明确的手势问道：“谁能说出我们之间有任何区别？”

在此之前，松井将军表示他对中日关系的未来持乐观态度，尽管他承认泛亚主义的实现需要时间。

松井将军是今日外交部长张群将军举行的午宴上的主宾。明日他将拜会行政院院长蒋介石将军。周日他将前往上海，会见中国银行董事会主席宋子文先生和大上海市长吴铁城先生。他将于3月18日从上海乘船前往日本。

不去北方

松井将军此次不访问华北。当被问及是否因为华北无需促进更好的中日关系时，他意味深长地笑着反问道：“华北的问题难道不是都已经解决了吗？”

March 11, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

Sin Wan Pao Evening Edition published the following comment on March 9:-

SINO-JAPANESE FRIENDSHIP

A letter from Foochow states that after arriving in Fokien, Matsui told pressmen that he would make a tour to conduct propaganda on Pan-Asiaticism. He added that in order to promote friendship between China and Japan, Chinese and Japanese should both come to their senses.

We are glad to hear of this, but for friendship to be maintained between Chinese and Japanese, sincerity is essential. Persons who talk loudly about the maintenance of friendship must correct their mistakes of the past.

In order to bring about good relations between China and Japan, good feeling between the two peoples must first be restored. Any person who sees his own fellow-country being insulted or oppressed will not be able to overcome his indignation. China never had any intention to be hostile towards Japan. HOW WE SHOULD CONDUCT OURSELVES AT THIS TIME OF NATIONAL CRISIS

At the present time when the situation in the Far East is most critical and the atmosphere in Europe is daily becoming more strained because of Germany's action, how should China conduct herself?

The other day, General Goering of Germany said, "To-day is the first day on which Germany has begun to recover her full freedom and Baron Lichtofen, who died for his country, can now close his eyes".

Sarraut, the French Premier, recently broadcasted a speech in which he said that the French people must now give up all internal dissensions and unite to support the Government.

There is a deadly enmity between Germany and France and both will play prominent parts in the second world war.

The above two speeches will serve as a lesson to our people. Conditions in China to-day are somewhat similar to those in Germany after the Great War. After a hard struggle for 18 years, Germany has released herself of her bonds. Such a spirit should be emulated by the Chinese people. We should always keep in mind the spirit of the German people.

Shun Pao publishes the following comment :-

A Pan-Asiatic League.

General Matsui of Japan is at present touring Kwangtung and Kwangsi where he is paying visits to political and military leaders in South China. According to General Matsui, his object is to discuss with Chinese leaders the question of establishing a Pan-Asiatic League.
Of late, Japanese government leaders have been advocating the principle of Pan Asiatism, but its object in advocating this principle is not to promote the welfare of all Asiatic races. It has long been the ambition of Japan to drive away European and American influences, political, military, economic and cultural, from Asia, with the Suez Canal as the dividing line between Japanese power and European influence.
The so-called Sino-Japanese League will be the predecessor of the Pan-Asiatic League and China will later be converted into a protectorate under Japan. If Japan really intends to emancipate the Asiatic races, how is she to explain the conditions now prevailing in Korea and Formosa? If Japan really intends to promote Asiatic culture, how is it that Japan is enforcing an education fit only for slaves in the Four North-Eastern Provinces and East Hopei? If Japan is sincere in her wish to render economic assistance to the Asiatic races, why has Japan adopted an aggressive trade policy in the Far East?
Under these circumstances, to advocate Pan-Asiatism will only create ill feeling among the peoples of Asia and expose Japan's cunning and deceit.

December 4, 1935.

Journal de Shanghai (Editorial) :

THE PAN-ASIATIC LEAGUE.

A Pan-Asiatic League has been formed at Tientsin. The principal members of the League are mostly former high Chinese officials. The Chairman is Li Sheng To, ex-Minister to Japan, and the Vice Chairman are Kao Ling Wei, formerly Director of the Maritime Customs at Peking, and General Chi Hai Yuan, formerly Inspector-General of Kiangsu, Kiangsi and Anhwei.

The object of the League is to propagate a notion of the solidarity of the Asiatic nations of which "China is the largest and Japan the strongest."

This is not the first time that a Pan-Asiatic movement has been reported. It has been to the fore for about 30 years. Long before the Great War, William II of Germany was alarmed at the enormous number of Asiatics in the Far East and denounced it as the Yellow Peril which he envisaged in the shape of an immense army invading Europe one day like the Huns and the Mongols.

The Pan-Asiatic doctrine began to spread in Japan after the Russo-Japanese War of 1904-1905. Japanese intellectuals and militarists preached the necessity of an alliance of all Asiatic races. Only, what they desired above everything else is that Japan must dominate the Asiatic Union by being its promoter, its guide and the beneficiary.

It is probable that while propagating the Pan-Asiatic doctrine beyond the borders of their country, the Japanese believe that they are working in the interests of other Asiatic peoples. They want to improve the life of the impoverished and "oppressed" races; they dream of releasing them from the tutelage of the West, only to replace it with Japanese tutelage.

They have perhaps secured sincere adherents in nationalist intellectual circles in certain countries of Asia, generally far away from Japan; they have also won the approval of idealists and dreamers. But it may be said that the Pan-Asiatic movement has not had, up to the present, practical application.

Japan has conducted an energetic propaganda in India but India will have little to gain should Japanese Pan-Asiaticism materialize. India has different castes. The fact that important relations exist between India and Japan is not sufficient cause for a political union to follow.

The relations between China and Japan have become more strained. For centuries, China had exercised a tremendous influence on Japanese civilization and for more than half a century Japan, in turn, has wielded as much influence over Young China as has the West. The relations between the two countries undergo frequent changes but during the past four years they have entered a critical stage and to-day we are witnessing one of the most important phases.

《上海日报》（社论）：

泛亚联盟。

一个泛亚联盟已在天津成立。该联盟的主要成员大多为前中国高官。主席为前驻日本公使李盛铎，副主席为前北京海关税务司高凌蔚，以及前江苏、江西和安徽巡阅使齐燮元将军。

该联盟的宗旨是宣扬亚洲各国团结的理念，其中“中国最大，日本最强”。

这并非首次报道泛亚运动。该运动已活跃约30年。早在世界大战之前，德国威廉二世就对远东庞大的亚洲人口感到震惊，并将其斥为“黄祸”，他设想这支大军会像匈人和蒙古人一样，有朝一日入侵欧洲。

泛亚主义学说在1904-1905年日俄战争后开始在日本传播。日本知识分子和军国主义者鼓吹所有亚洲种族结盟的必要性。只不过，他们最渴望的是日本必须通过成为推动者、引导者和受益者来主导亚洲联盟。

很可能，日本人在向国外传播泛亚主义学说时，相信他们是在为其他亚洲人民的利益行事。他们希望改善贫困和受“压迫”种族的生活；他们梦想将这些种族从西方的监护下解放出来，只是为了用日本的监护取而代之。

December 4, 1935. Afternoon Translation.

Journal de Shanghai (Editorial) :

THE PAN-ASIATIC LEAGUE.

A Pan-Asiatic League has been formed at Tientsin. The principal members of the League are mostly former high Chinese officials. The Chairman is Li Sheng To, ex-Minister to Japan, and the Vice Chairmen are Kao Ling Wei, formerly Director of the Maritime Customs at Peking, and General Chi Hsi Yuan, formerly Inspector-General of Kiangsu, Kiangsi and Anhwei.

The object of the League is to propagate a notion of the solidarity of the Asiatic nations of which "China is the largest and Japan the strongest."

This is not the first time that a Pan-Asiatic movement has been reported. It has been to the fore for about 30 years. Long before the Great War, William II of Germany was alarmed at the enormous number of Asiatics in the Far East and denounced it as the Yellow Peril which he envisaged in the shape of an immense army invading Europe one day like the Huns and the Mongols.

The Pan-Asiatic doctrine began to spread in Japan after the Russo-Japanese War of 1904-1905. Japanese intellectuals and militarists preached the necessity of an alliance of all Asiatic races. Only, what they desired above everything else is that Japan must dominate the Asiatic Union by being its promoter, its guide and the beneficiary.

It is probable that while propagating the Pan-Asiatic doctrine beyond the borders of their country, the Japanese believe that they are working in the interests of other Asiatic peoples. They want to improve the life of the impoverished and "oppressed" races; they dream of releasing them from the tutelage of the West, only to replace it with Japanese tutelage.

They have perhaps secured sincere adherents in nationalist intellectual circles in certain countries of Asia, generally far away from Japan; they have also won the approval of idealists and dreamers. But it may be said that the Pan-Asiatic movement has not had, up to the present, practical application.

Japan has conducted an energetic propaganda in India but India will have little to gain should Japanese Pan-Asiaticism materialize. India has different castes. The fact that important relations exist between India and Japan is not sufficient cause for a political union to follow.

The relations between China and Japan have become more strained. For centuries, China had exercised a tremendous influence on Japanese civilization and for more than half a century Japan, in turn, has wielded as much influence over Young China as has the West. The relations between the two countries undergo frequent changes but during the past four years they have entered a critical stage and to-day we are witnessing one of the most important phases.

Recently, an Indo-Japanese Association was established at Kobe whose avowed object is to bring the two peoples into closer touch. All persons who desire to see the "two sister nations walk hand in hand, free, happy, prosperous and peaceful" are invited to join the Association.
"We know nothing about India", states a manifesto issued by the founders of the Association, "and India knows nothing about us, or rather an ill-omened propaganda is telling the Indians that Japan is an imperialist nation, that she has invaded Manchuria, that she desires to impose her will upon the whole of Asia, that she is exploiting the markets of India and is working harm to her prosperity."
After relating the historic relations between the two countries, the manifesto recalls that it was India which gave Buddha to Japan and points out the necessity of developing more and more the religious, cultural and commercial relations between the two countries.
All this is, of course, intended to win the hearts of the Indian people so that they might throw open their markets to Japanese goods.
Amongst other passages contained in the manifesto, we quote the following :- "We have been too long unconscious of the misery of our 350,000,000 Indian brothers and sisters who are suffering under the unjust and unjustifiable yoke of the British who are exploiting them."
According to this passage in the manifesto, it seems that the object of the Association is not only to develop commercial relations with India but also to support the anti-British opposition. We cannot say whether there are any influential Japanese behind the founders of the Indo-Japanese Association. It may have been initiated by certain intellectuals or merchants. However, the political character which they are giving to the Association should not escape the notice of the Japanese authorities.
The Association should understand that nothing can be gained by its action in provoking domestic troubles among its neighbours. Above all, Japan should not overlook the fact that if she carries out intrigues in other countries, they could do the same in some part of her colonies. “我们对印度一无所知”，该协会发起人在一份宣言中 stated，“印度也对我们一无所知，或者说，一种不祥的宣传正在告诉印度人，日本是一个帝国主义国家，它侵占了满洲，企图将其意志强加于整个亚洲，它正在剥削印度市场并损害其繁荣。”
在叙述了两国之间的历史关系后，该宣言回顾说是印度将佛陀传给了日本，并指出有必要进一步发展两国之间的宗教、文化和商业关系。
当然，这一切旨在赢得印度人民的民心，以便他们向日本商品开放市场。
在宣言包含的其他段落中，我们引用如下：“我们长期以来一直无视我们3.5亿印度兄弟姐妹的痛苦，他们正遭受着剥削他们的英国人不公正且毫无道理的统治。”
根据宣言中的这一段，该协会的目的似乎不仅是发展与印度的商业关系，还支持反英反对派。我们无法断定印日协会发起人背后是否有有影响力的日本人支持。该协会可能由某些知识分子或商人发起。然而，他们赋予该协会的政治性质不应被日本当局忽视。
该协会应当明白，通过行动挑起邻国内乱是得不到任何好处的。最重要的是，日本不应忽视这样一个事实：如果她在其他国家搞阴谋诡计，别人也可以在她的殖民地的某些地方如法炮制。因此，各国最好彼此采取适当的态度，不要为了挑起邻国麻烦而策划任何阴谋。

G. M.

A GENERAL VIEW OF INDIA

Reports on the Indian people's struggle for
liberty and independence are appearing from time to time
in various Japanese newspapers. The public has been
greatly misled regarding the culture and characteristics
of Indians. Are Indians, as has been propagated by the
British people, uncivilized? Is India degenerating?
India is an ancient country having been founded
in the days of Moses and Pharoah. Its population is
greater than the combined population of North and South
America. The Indian people were already highly civilized
when the Europeans were still in an uncivilized state.
Almost all countries in the world owe much to Indian
civilization. India was the country which defeated the
ambition of Alexander the Great. India produced one of
the three great religions and is the birth-place of two
of the worlds greatest poets. Kalidasa (?), who is
generally regarded as the Shakespeare of the Orient, was
born in India. The invention of the decimal system,
which is the basis of mathematics and the fundamentals
of modern chemistry were the work of an Indian. Thus
India is the country which made the present world
civilization possible and she deserves to be called
"The foundation of all the sciences".
At present India is under slavery, yet she
has produced many well known scholars such as Drs.
Tagore and Raman, who won the noble prize a few years ago.
Indian architecture is equal to that of the
ancient Greeks and Romans and her temple architecture
is well known throughout the world.

印度概览

关于印度人民争取自由和独立斗争的报道不时出现在各种日本报纸上。公众对于印度人的文化和特征产生了极大的误解。印度人是否像英国人所宣传的那样未开化？印度是否在退化？
印度是一个古老的国家，建于摩西和法老时代。其人口超过北美和南美人口的总和。当欧洲人仍处于未开化状态时，印度人民已经高度文明。世界上几乎所有国家都受惠于印度文明。印度是挫败亚历山大大帝野心的国家。印度产生了世界三大宗教之一，也是两位世界最伟大诗人的诞生地。通常被视为东方莎士比亚的迦梨陀娑（Kalidasa，?）就出生在印度。十进制系统的发明——这是数学的基础以及现代化学的基本原理——是一位印度人的成果。因此，印度是使当今世界文明成为可能的国家，她理应被称为“所有科学的基础”。
目前印度虽处于奴役之下，但仍涌现出许多著名学者，如几年前获得诺贝尔奖的泰戈尔博士（Dr. Tagore）和拉曼博士（Dr. Raman）。
印度建筑可与古希腊和古罗马建筑相媲美，其寺庙建筑闻名于世。

“Make Me Your Leader!” Japan Urges Asia

With the organization of the Pan-Asiatic League at Tokyo, soon to be inaugurated, Japan seeks to draw China, Siam, India, and the Near East into a league to line up half the world’s population against Great Britain. “Make me your leader,” Japan declares, “and I will, with my powerful army and navy, free you from the shackles of the West.” In the article published below, Mr. Hollington Tong describes the growth of this movement which, he declares, will “guide them to a goal of utter ruin and destruction.” The vast territory Japan seeks to draw together against the West is seen at a glance on the above map.

While distinguished statesmen from many countries at a London conference are searching for a panacea to terminate the world economic depression, an event of profound import which may bring one stage nearer the much-feared clash between Eastern and Western civilisations is to take place in Japan during the next few days. The Pan-Asiatic League will soon be inaugurated under the patronage of many powerful Japanese leaders in Tokyo, which in consequence may in the eyes of future historians outshine Geneva.

The immediate object of the league is to line up all the Asiatic peoples, nearly half of the world’s population, against Great Britain on account of her policy to restrict Japanese imports into her colonial possessions. It is evident that the British abrogation of the 1911 trade convention between Japan and India in April last, an increase in the Siam government in the increased minimum specific duty on cotton plain-grey goods of non-British origin from 50 to 75 per cent ad valorem on June 1 have incensed the Japanese almost to the breaking point.

Racial War Declared

They have enlisted the support of all the Indian revolutionists in Japan and other countries in the anti-British movement. Members of the Young League as well as those of the nationalist party of India, whose activities in Japan were hitherto restricted have been given freedom of expression. In fact the Japanese police who used to dog every footstep of these Indian refugees are literally fraternising with them.

随着即将在东京成立的泛亚联盟，日本试图将中国、暹罗、印度和近东纳入一个联盟，使世界一半的人口站在大英帝国的对立面。“让我做你们的领袖，”日本宣称，“我将凭借我强大的海陆军，把你们从西方的枷锁中解放出来。”在下文发表的文章中，董显光先生描述了这一运动的发展，他称该运动将“引导他们走向彻底毁灭和破坏的终点”。日本企图联合起来对抗西方的广阔领土，在上方的地图上一目了然。

东西方冲突被煽动

当来自许多国家的杰出政治家在伦敦会议上寻找终结世界经济萧条的灵丹妙药时，一件具有深远意义的事件将在未来几天内于日本发生，这可能使人们更加 feared 的东西方文明之间的冲突又逼近了一步。泛亚联盟不久将在东京众多有权势的日本领导人的支持下成立，因此在未来的历史学家眼中，其光芒可能会盖过日内瓦。

该联盟的直接目标是让所有亚洲人民——几乎占世界人口的一半——联合起来反对大英帝国，原因是英国限制日本进口到其殖民地的政策。显然，去年四月英国废除1911年日印贸易公约，以及暹罗政府于6月1日将非英产原色平纹棉布的最低特定关税从50%提高到75%，这些举动激怒了日本人，几乎使其达到破裂的边缘。

作为报复，日本人显然已向大英帝国宣战，发动了种族战争。他们争取到了在日本和其他国家的全体印度革命者对反英运动的支持。此前在日本活动受到限制的印度青年联盟成员以及印度国民党成员，现在已获准自由表达观点。事实上，过去对这些印度流亡者步步紧逼的日本警察，现在简直是在与他们称兄道弟。

三月，大东亚协会成立。该协会在东京会馆举行开幕式，特意选择3月1日——即所谓“满洲国”成立一周年纪念日——作为协会成立之日，其目标之一是在日本领导下统一亚洲人民，这显示了日本人缺乏幽默感，并再次证明他们无法理解其他亚洲人民的心理。

据两位发起人木村马林（Barin Kimura，音译）和冈仓博士（Dr. Okakura，音译）概述，新协会的主要工作是努力传播和宣扬日本文化，并通过广播他们的文化、组织讲座、会议和发行小册子来促进亚洲人民的觉醒。然而，众所周知的秘密是，该协会的真正动机是将日本的影响力扩展到亚洲的各个角落。

The leaders of the Asiatic Anti-British Society include a number of rabid anti-British Indians among whom is Rash Behari Bose, who is a Japanese subject, and a member of the Black Dragon Society. The president of the society is Mr. Tamon Yokota, who is also chairman of the Japan Peasants' Federation. Offices are maintained in the Uchisaiwai-cho quarter of Tokyo, a section of the city quite popular with politicians.

Ever since the abrogation of the Indo-Japanese trade convention, this organization has become greatly concerned with the sufferings of the Indians under British "inhuman" policies. Mr. Yokota declared on one occasion: "Of India's population of 350,000,000, more than 80 per cent are farmers and, when Japanese goods are excluded from India, these will be forced to buy Lancashire manufactures at higher prices. If Japan retaliates, the Indian people would suffer greatly. Must we look on, with arms folded, while such heinous acts are committed?"

Dr. Gorai Active

The origin of the Asiatic Anti-British Society could be traced to the activities of Dr. Gorai, who has been described as one of the noisiest and most bellicose of the university professors in Tokyo. Early in the year, he urged that no time be lost in forming an eastern league of Asiatics to be pitted against the League of Nations. He also pictured Great Britain as a fiend incarnate, a veritable Machiavelli. He said: "Not China, not America, but Britain is the enemy, yet the Japanese do not seem to be able to see this." It may also be recalled that about the same time Mr. Matsuoka, Japan's former chief delegate to Geneva, threatened Great Britain with dire consequences for her failure to support Japan.

Dr. Gorai, elsewhere described as a well-known reactionary professor of Waseda University, is one of the advisers of the Kodokai ("Imperial Way Society"), an organization largely composed of militarists and members of right wing farmers' unions, who are interested in overthrowing the white races and in promoting the hegemony of Japan among the Asiatic races.

There seems to have been a plethora of societies in Japan for the promotion of the Asia idea. A few weeks ago a patriotic body called the Asia Seinen Doshikai (Asiatic Young Men's Society) was organized in Kobe. At the time of its inauguration the following planks were adopted:
"1. Acting in the spirit on which our nation was founded, we will do our utmost to establish our racial idea;
"2. Release the peoples of Asia from the shackles of the white man's control; and
"3. Destroy capitalism, the international weapon devised for the white man's benefit alone and the old-established political parties."

Conference Planned

The promoters of the Great Asia Association in the welter of confusion caused by various Asia societies saw the opportunity of creating the Pan-Asiatic League. They have planned to hold a conference for the formal organization of the league during the next few days in Tokyo, which tends to unify all efforts presently directed against Great Britain and later against other Western countries which should try to thwart Japan's aspiration for a trade monopoly in Asia.

Behind this league movement stand Prince Konoe, vice-president of the House of Peers, Admiral Viscount Ogasawara, Mr. Hirota, former ambassador to Russia, Lieutenant-General Matsui, Baron Ekuchi and Dr. Murakawa, professor of the Tokyo Imperial University, who have openly identified themselves with it. General Araki, minister of war, Admiral Kato, former chief of the naval general staff, and General Honjo, former commander of the Kwantung Garrison, are sympathizers with the movement though they have not actively associated themselves with it.

The inaugural meeting for the league, it is claimed, will be attended by delegates from all the Asiatic countries. Several Indian leaders with whom the writer has conversed on the subject called special attention to the possible attendance of a brother of the king of Siam at the conference. Despite the smallness of her territory Siam seems destined to play an important part in the Pan-Asiatic movement made in Japan.

After having refrained from voting on the League's resolution concerning the Chinese-Japanese controversy, Siam's friendly relationship with Japan has increased to such an extent that some learned Japanese has established a blood kinship of the Japanese with the Siamese. Professor Onji Azuma, of Tokyo has found remains of quite a large Japanese colony in Siam, which existed, so it is said, less than 200 years ago, but has since been absorbed into the Siamese race. This reminds one of the Japanese attempts to prove kinship with the Mexicans back in 1914. Similarly they find themselves related to the Mongols and the Malaya peoples.

From a small but powerful group of Indians in Shanghai to whom the Japanese have unfolded their secret designs to expel British rule and influence from Asia, it is also learned that the Chinese will be represented by several politicians of the southwest at the conference. The names of these politicians, it is explained, are to be kept absolutely confidential for fear that their disclosure might have bad repercussions upon themselves in the present temper of the Chinese people. There is speculation in some quarters as to the identity of the Chinese representatives, but it may be desirable not to go further into this matter.

Prominent Men Interested

The Japanese foreign office is understood to be tremendously interested in the league conference. Mr. Uchida, minister of foreign affairs, and Mr. Yoshizawa, former Japanese minister to China, as honorary advisers of the league are, the writer presumes, doing everything within their power to make the movement a success. Naturally it will be of considerable interest to know how many delegates from the Asiatic countries other than Japan will attend. The organizing committee of the Pan-Asiatic League boasts of the sure presence of representatives from China, India, the Philippines, Persia, Siam and Afghanistan. Although Egypt is in Africa, she has also been invited to be represented at the conference.

The league in the course of formation has already a monthly publication to advance its interests. The magazine is called "Pan-Asianism," its first issue being published on May 1. It contained a very interesting article from General Araki, minister of war, in which he discussed eloquently Japan's mission to save Asia from the yoke of white men and declared that the key to peace on this continent is held by his country. Mr. Yoshizawa, who has hitherto been reluctant to contribute articles to the press, was credited with a short article on Pan-Asianism in which he pointed out that the time is ripe for the movement of "Asia for Asiatics." General Honjo's congratulatory message received a prominent place in the magazine.

The magazine further contained information about the interest of southwestern Chinese in the movement. It is said that many overseas Chinese have been enthusiastic supporters of Japanese leadership in Asia and that a similar movement has been started by members of the Kuomintang in Canton. The promoters of the league also tried to link it with Dr. Sun Yat-sen, who was represented by them to favor Pan-Asiatic activities.

Sounds Warning

In January, Captain Wedgwood Benn, former secretary of state for India, speaking on Oriental affairs at Toronto, had sufficient vision to see that the difficulties of the eastern situation lay in the possibility that Japan might secure the leadership of the East against the West rather than in the result of a Sino-Japanese conflict and that the vital question is whether India, in bridging the gap between the East and the West, will be able to bear the strain.

This might be described as the warning of a realist. Japan stands today as stood Mahomed—with a sword in one hand and the Koran in the other. But instead of the Koran Japan clutches the cult of Pan-Asianism, with herself as the leader. Those Asiatic nations who do not accept the cult will be put to the sword, those who accept it will have the honor of being humble bearers of her train. In effect Japan calls to the other Asiatic nations:—"Make me your leader, and I with my powerful army and navy will free you from the shackles of the West."

To those whose ignoble love of temporary ease and peace blinds them to the terrible possibilities of ghastly and protracted bloodshed that the Pan-Asiatic movement under the leadership of Japan would inevitably open up, the Japanese offer may make a strong appeal. But fortunately there are but few in China who do not realize that Japanese leadership would guide them to a goal of utter ruin and destruction.

亚洲反英社的领导层包括数名狂热的反英印度人，其中就有拉什·比哈里·博斯（Rash Behari Bose），他是日本臣民，也是黑龙会成员。该社社长是横田多门（Tamon Yokota）先生，他同时也是日本农民联合会主席。该社在东京内幸町区设有办事处，该区是政客们颇为青睐的地段。

自从印日贸易协定废止以来，该组织便极大地关注印度人在英国“不人道”政策下所遭受的苦难。横田先生曾宣称：“在印度三亿五千万人口中，超过百分之八十是农民，当日本商品被排除出印度市场时，这些人将被迫以更高的价格购买兰开夏郡的制造品。如果日本进行报复，印度人民将遭受巨大苦难。面对如此令人发指的行径，我们难道能袖手旁观吗？”

五来井博士的活动

亚洲反英社的起源可追溯至五来井（Gorai）博士的活动，他被描述为东京大学中最聒噪、最好战的教授之一。今年年初，他敦促应立即成立一个东方亚洲人联盟，以对抗国际联盟。他还把英国描绘成恶魔的化身，一个真正的马基雅维利式人物。他说：“敌人不是中国，也不是美国，而是英国，但日本人似乎未能看清这一点。”人们或许还记得，大约在同一时间，日本前驻日内瓦首席代表松冈洋右先生威胁英国称，若不支持日本，将面临严重后果。

五来井博士在其他地方也被描述为早稻田大学著名的反动派教授，他是弘道会（“皇道会”）的顾问之一，该组织主要由军国主义分子和右翼农民工会成员组成，他们热衷于推翻白人种族，并促进日本在亚洲种族中的霸权地位。

日本似乎充斥着各种宣扬“亚洲主义”理念的社团。几周前，一个名为“亚细亚青年同志会”（Asia Seinen Doshikai，即亚洲青年协会）的爱国团体在神户成立。在其成立之际，通过了以下纲领：
“1. 本着建国精神，我们将竭尽全力确立我们的种族理念；
“2. 将亚洲人民从白人的控制枷锁中解放出来；以及
“3. 摧毁资本主义——这种仅为白人利益而设计的国际武器，以及旧有的政党。”

计划召开会议

大亚细亚协会的发起者在各种亚洲社团造成的混乱局面中，看到了创建泛亚联盟的机会。他们计划在未来几天于东京举行会议，正式成立该联盟，旨在统一目前针对英国的所有努力，并在日后针对那些试图阻碍日本在亚洲建立贸易垄断野心的其他西方国家。

在这个联盟运动背后站着的有贵族院副议长近卫公爵、小笠原海军中将子爵、前驻俄大使广田弘毅先生、松井陆军中将、江口男爵以及东京帝国大学教授村川博士，他们都已公开表示支持。陆军大臣荒木贞夫大将、前海军军令部总长加藤宽治海军大将以及前关东军司令官本庄繁大将虽未积极参与，但对该运动持同情态度。

据称，联盟的成立大会将有来自所有亚洲国家的代表出席。几位就此议题与笔者交谈过的印度领导人特别提请注意，暹罗国王的兄弟可能会出席会议。尽管暹罗领土狭小，但它似乎注定要在日本发起的泛亚运动中扮演重要角色。

在 abstain（弃权）投票反对国际联盟关于中日争端的决议后，暹罗与日本的友好关系已发展到如此程度，以至于一些日本学者建立了日本人与暹罗人之间的血缘亲属关系。东京的东恩寺（Onji Azuma，音译）教授在暹罗发现了相当规模的日本侨民聚居地的遗迹，据说该聚居地存在于不到200年前，但此后已被同化入暹罗种族。这让人想起日本人在1914年试图证明与墨西哥人有亲属关系的举动。同样地，他们也发现自己与蒙古人和马来人有着亲缘关系。

从上海的一小群但颇具影响力的印度人那里也得知，日本人向他们透露了将英国统治和势力逐出亚洲的秘密计划，这些人还透露，西南地区的几名政客将在会议上代表中国。据解释，这些政客的名字必须绝对保密，以免在当前中国人民的情绪下，泄露身份会对他们自身产生不良反响。某些方面对中国代表的身份有所猜测，但在此问题上不宜深究更为妥当。

显要人士的关注

据悉，日本外务省对此次联盟会议极为关注。笔者认为，外务大臣内田康哉先生和前日本驻华公使吉泽健吉先生作为联盟的名誉顾问，正在尽其所能推动该运动取得成功。自然，有多少除日本以外的亚洲国家代表出席将是颇受关注的问题。泛亚联盟的组织委员会夸口称，中国、印度、菲律宾、波斯、暹罗和阿富汗的代表肯定会出席。虽然埃及位于非洲，但也受邀派代表参加会议。

该联盟在组建过程中已经拥有一份月刊以推进其利益。该杂志名为《泛亚主义》（Pan-Asianism），首期于5月1日出版。其中刊登了一篇来自陆军大臣荒木大将的非常有趣的文章，他在文中雄辩地论述了日本将亚洲从白人枷锁中拯救出来的使命，并宣称掌握这片大陆和平钥匙的是他的国家。此前一直不愿向媒体投稿的吉泽先生，也被认为撰写了一篇关于泛亚主义的短文，指出“亚洲人的亚洲”运动的时机已经成熟。本庄大将的贺词在杂志中占据了显著位置。

该杂志还包含了关于中国西南地区对该运动感兴趣的信息。据说许多海外华侨一直是日本领导亚洲的热情支持者，且国民党的成员在广州也发起了类似的运动。联盟的发起者还试图将其与孙中山博士联系起来，声称孙博士支持泛亚活动。

发出警告

今年一月，前印度事务大臣韦奇伍德·本恩上校（Captain Wedgwood Benn）在多伦多就东方事务发表演讲时，具有足够的远见看出，东方局势的困难在于日本可能获得对抗西方的东方领导权，而非中日冲突的结果，并且关键问题在于印度在弥合东西方差距时，能否承受住这种压力。

这可以被描述为现实主义者发出的警告。今天的日本就像穆罕默德当年一样——一手持剑，一手持《古兰经》。但日本手中紧握的不是《古兰经》，而是以自身为领袖的泛亚主义信条。那些不接受这一信条的亚洲国家将遭到剑刃相加，而那些接受者则将荣幸地成为谦卑的追随者。实际上，日本向其他亚洲国家呼吁：“让我做你们的领袖，我将凭借强大的海陆军力量，将你们从西方的枷锁中解放出来。”

对于那些因卑劣地贪图暂时的安逸与和平而对日本领导下的泛亚运动必然引发的可怕且持久的血腥屠杀可能性视而不见的人来说，日本的提议可能具有强烈的吸引力。但幸运的是，在中国，意识到日本领导会将他们引向彻底毁灭深渊的人并非少数。

COPY 65

Anti-British Posters Make
Appearance In Japan

Charge Of Ingratitude Despite Japan's Fidelity
To Anglo-Japanese Alliance During War;
Unknown Body As The Author

TOKYO, May 1. — Denouncing Britain for its allegedly perfidious treatment of its old ally Japan, posters conspicuously printed in black, white, and red have recently appeared pasted on wooden hoardings, fences and telegraph poles throughout the city of Tokyo. Bold characters in white on a black background credit a hitherto unknown organization, styling itself the "Asiatic Anti-British League," with the authorship.

After charging Britain with ingratitude towards Japan despite Japan's fidelity to the Anglo-Japanese Alliance during the Great War, these posters accuse Britain of having compelled Japan to accept an inadequate naval ratio at the Washington Conference and of fostering anti-Japanese sentiment at Geneva. In conclusion, they demand the emancipation of India from British rule and call on "the 400,000,000 people of China and the 300,000,000 people of India to drive British influence west of Suez."

In view of this concluding demand, it would probably be safe to hazard the guess that the prime movers in this new "League" are the handful of India malcontents and political refugees, led by the well-known seditionist Rash Bihari Bose, who play so active a part in trying to stir up anti-British sentiment in Japan under the guise of Pan-Asianism. Neither the "League" nor the posters issued in its name should, therefore, be taken too seriously, though there is no denying the fact that considerable resentment against Britain is felt just at present even among Japanese normally friendly to England.

The abrogation of the Anglo-Japanese Alliance in 1922 has always rankled with the Japanese, but they have done their best to hide their ruffled feelings by maintaining that, dead as the Alliance may now be in fact, it yet remains as alive as ever in spirit. It came as a sad blow to them, therefore, when Britain recorded her vote along with those of the other 41 nations which voted against Japan at the League Assembly in February.

One Thing After Another

On top of this has come the notification of the Indian Government's intention to abrogate the Indo-Japan Commercial Convention. Like the case of the Anglo-Japanese Alliance, this cancellation has come—or so it seems to most Japanese—just at the moment when the treaty has ceased to give the main advantage to Britain; for no Japanese can be brought to believe that the abrogation is intended for India's good. Lancashire, not India, is the real instigator of abrogation, they assert. They are equally convinced that Britain, through the medium of the Indian Government, is in reality merely camouflaging its true intention, which is to bring economic pressure to bear on Japan and thereby assist the League to enforce the decisions reached at Geneva, in February.—Reuter.

东京，5月1日电。——谴责英国据称背信弃义地对待其老盟友日本，最近，用黑、白、红三色醒目印刷的海报出现在东京全市的木板围墙、栅栏和电线杆上。黑色背景上的白色大字将一个迄今未知的组织署名为作者，该组织自称为“亚洲反英联盟”。

在指责英国尽管日本在大战期间忠于英日同盟却仍对日本忘恩负义之后，这些海报指控英国迫使日本在华盛顿会议上接受不充分的海军比例，并在日内瓦煽动反日情绪。最后，它们要求将印度从英国统治下解放出来，并呼吁“四亿中国人民和三亿印度人民将英国势力驱逐至苏伊士运河以西”。

鉴于这一最终要求，大胆猜测这一新“联盟”的主要推动者是少数印度不满分子和政治难民可能是安全的，他们由著名的煽动者拉什·比哈里·博斯领导，在泛亚主义的幌子下积极试图在日本煽动反英情绪。因此，无论是该“联盟”还是以它的名义发布的海报，都不应过于当真，尽管不可否认的事实是，即使在通常对英国友好的日本人中，目前也对英国怀有相当大的怨恨。

1922年英日同盟的废止一直让日本人耿耿于怀，但他们尽力掩饰这种不快的情绪，坚称尽管同盟在事实上可能已经死亡，但在精神上依然鲜活。因此，当英国在二月的国联大会上与其他41个投票反对日本的国家一起投下反对票时，这对他们来说是一个沉重的打击。

接二连三的事件

在此之上，又传来了印度政府打算废止印日商业协定的通知。与英日同盟的情况一样，这次废止发生的时间——至少在大多数日本人看来——正是在条约不再给英国带来主要优势的时刻；因为没有日本人会相信废止协定是为了印度的利益。他们断言，兰开夏郡而非印度才是废止协定的真正策动者。他们同样确信，英国通过印度政府这一媒介，实际上只是在掩盖其真实意图，即对日本施加经济压力，从而协助国联执行二月在日内瓦达成的决定。——路透社。
